A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PanoHead-based head-stylization framework. All 13 pages of v1.pdf and 17 pages of v2.pdf, including their appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original stylization experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations and a 25-participant user study.

after.justification: Original experiments are retained and expanded with additional comparators, checkpoint and rank analyses, KID scores and runtime results. The user study remains in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains LD, fixed rank weighting, mirror gradients, grid distillation and bypassing super-resolution layers for grid gradients. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. Clarifications about CFG and omitting PlacidDreamer's additional optimization do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The FFHQ-based head-stylization coverage is retained. v2 adds Caricature and Oil Painting examples in Figure 14, while removing the Metallic face paint example from v1 Figure 9. Charcoal in the new figure matches the existing sketch task.

E2.justification: v2 adds InstructPix2Pix and InstantID to Table 1, and both plus Instruct-NeRF2NeRF to Figure 8. Figure 3 newly evaluates PlacidDreamer's additions against LD and the full method; v1 only cited that work. The four original main baselines remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds KID evaluation on the existing test set and compares weighted versus unweighted distillation across SD1.5, RV3.0, RV5.1 and SDXL. The stated 10k-iteration training setup and approximately 100-image test set remain. Table 2 drops its explicit prompt-averaging description, preventing confirmation of whether that experiment's settings changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds LD versus PlacidDreamer diagnostics, checkpoint sensitivity in Figure 4, cumulative rank-k comparisons across styles in Figure 14, and accessory-preservation failures in Figure 12. Table 2 also replaces the quantitative component-ablation evidence. These substantially expand examination of the method's behavior.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly specifies that the 2D methods use the same seed across views. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; this seed disclosure does not establish additional repeated experiments.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 rows and user-study results are unchanged, but v2 adds comparator scores, KID results, runtimes and qualitative outcomes. Table 2 extensively replaces values: final FID/CLIP/ID changes from 82.3/0.80/0.72 to 84.17/0.86/0.52, with matched aggregation unconfirmed. Within the reported ablations, adding mirror gradients improves FID from 85.7 to 82.3 in v1 but worsens it from 81.11 to 84.17 in v2.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly gives an explicit mathematical definition of the SDS gradient, including timestep weighting and the renderer Jacobian, in v2 Equation (6). The proposed LD, mirror-pose and joint-view derivations and Appendix A mathematics remain unchanged; one redundant chain-rule expansion is compressed.

C1.justification: The central identity-preserving, 360-degree stylization claims remain. v2 explicitly claims novelty in improving GAN identity preservation by changing distillation characteristics rather than adding losses, and presents rank weighting as a new means of controlling stylization.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges failures to preserve earrings and hair accessories and the generator's output-resolution limit. It adds an interpretation of rank-k reconstruction as controlling coarse/fine spatial content, discusses generalization across latent spaces, and explains the new Sketch FID-versus-KID comparison.

D1.justification: v2 discloses approximately three hours of tuning per prompt on one A100 GPU, approximately 0.5-second inference, and runtime/denoising-step information for added comparators. Existing implementation parameters and resource links remain. Conversely, Table 2 loses the specification that v1 averaged sketch, statue and werewolf prompts.

R1.justification: v2 adds InstructPix2Pix, Instruct-NeRF2NeRF, InstantID and an SDXL latent-space explanation, while removing GANSpace, Linearly Controllable GAN and Resolution Dependent GAN Interpolation. Rank weighting is repositioned around diffusion-latent color information, and the distinction from prior SDS regularization is emphasized.

P1.justification: v2 tightens introductory and methodological prose, adds a dedicated SDS-versus-LD discussion, and reorganizes supplementary material into additional User study and Additional results sections. The user study moves out of the main text, while the overall five-section narrative and much existing wording remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparison, sensitivity and failure panels, six supplementary comparison galleries, and a KID table. Table 1 gains grouped 2D/3D rows and color shading; Table 2 changes its highlighting. Existing displays are resized or relocated, including the user-study chart from Figure 6 to Figure 15, and the additional-prompt montage is shortened.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, checkpoint/rank analyses, KID results and illustrated failure cases make the validation and applicability claims more informative. The gain is limited by weaker ablation traceability: Table 2 changes its measurements and drops its averaging prompts, while the new mirror-gradient FID worsening remains undiscussed and receives favorable green delta highlighting.
